steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: Ugh... *sob*...

steps.name: Flustered Voice
steps.text: C-Calm down, sir!

steps.name: Flustered Voice
steps.text: Someone has already gone to get Operator Nowell! I-If you could move that needle away from her temple—

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: I'm not moving until he shows up.

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: But I suggest you avoid making any sudden moves.

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: Otherwise, I can't promise my hand will stay steady.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *pant*—*pant*—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I-I'm here. Who's... what happened—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: —Huh?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Mr. Nowell.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: That's me. And you are...?

steps.name: Flustered Operator
steps.text: Operator Nowell is here, Mr. Eroshka! Can you put the needle down now?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Your name is Eroshka?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You don't remember me...

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I shouldn't be surprised. I've changed a lot since we last met.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I'm sorry, I don't. But you wanted me, and I'm here. Can you let the hostage go now? You can have me instead.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I'm coming to you, slowly. Can you let go of the girl?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Come alone and stop two steps before me. Then I'll let go of her.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: No weapons.

steps.name: Flustered Operator
steps.text: Be careful, Mr. Nowell...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Alright.
Nowell puts down his Arts Unit and optometric equipment, gestures to the old man, and then starts walking forward.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: One more step.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've done as you said. Now—

steps.name: Frightened Operator
steps.text: Oh—!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Uh—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I'm a man of my word.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...I came to Rhodes Island at the recommendation of an old client after I left Londinium.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Rhodes Island is a pharmaceutical company specializing in Oripathy research and treatment. They have branches and clinics in many places. That's why I've resurfaced.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Oripathy. Hmph.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You cure uncurable diseases now?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: That's outside the scope of my work, and beyond my abilities.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Right. You're an optician, not a doctor.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've gained sufficient basic medical knowledge to save lives in the broad sense.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Someone who spent his entire life trying to die, now making it his life's work to save lives...

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Is this some kind of sick joke?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: It's no joke, Eroshka.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've said a lot. What about you? You didn't do all this just to remember old times with me, did you?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: If that was it, you wouldn't have to threaten these kids. They would have brought you to me.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Or are you simply being impulsive and dramatic, just like old times?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I never expected that would get you to recognize me so quickly.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Then why?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Because your people were taking down your tents and preparing to move out.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You know as well as I do why Oripathy clinics in Ursus operate like traveling circuses, ready to move at a moment's notice.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Yes, Oripathy, the Patrol Unit, the civil rights situation... same old story. That's not my point.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I came as soon as I heard you were here, only to see your people packing up and getting ready to leave.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Only the girl I held up was working in the tent up front. She apologized to me and said that you weren't taking patients, because you were moving elsewhere.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You're right. I should have told her I wasn't a patient, asked her if there was a man named Nowell here, and to take me to him.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: But I couldn't wait.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...Have you been searching for me?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I said, I'm a man of my word.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Wait, go no further.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Get out of my way! Let me go back!

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: I'm going back to them! Even if we die, we'll die together!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: There's no point.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Wh-What did you say?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: What's the point of going in there?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I get out of the way, you go into the fire and die with your family... no one will ever remember what happened here.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: That's better than being the only one to live! I'm not a coward!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Surely you understand what true cowardice would be.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Someone has to suffer the consequences of choosing the wrong side. But if the 'silencing' has taken place before the Emperor's edict—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Then the worst that can happen to those who survive this human-caused tragedy is exile.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Wh-What are you trying to say?!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Is it not clear enough? They sacrificed themselves to protect you.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Protect me? Ha... hahahaha! Protect me!

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: It was you, wasn't it? You're the one who killed them! And you say it was their choice, to protect me—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...Eroshka. That's your name?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Alors, Eroshka. I'm just a traveling optician. I'm not even from Ursus, and I have no interest in intervening in your conflicts.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I simply came to repay a favor. Your father asked me to save your life, and I did. That's all.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Do you think I would believe your shit—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: No, I thought you would be wiser. Impulsive and dramatic behavior is the privilege of the young, and you're not THAT young.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: ...I know it. It was you—it has to be you!

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: How could you know so much, if you were really just a simple optician?!

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Unless you were part of it to begin with...

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Yes, yes. That must be it!

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: I'm going to kill you.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: I'll kill you!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You're welcome to try. You'll earn my gratitude.
The soot has blackened the Ursus youth's hands. Without a second thought, he raises his only weapon and runs it through the unmoving man.
The dagger misses the man's heart and becomes stuck several inches under his ribs.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Damn—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Wh-Why didn't you dodge?!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Because, if you actually manage to kill me, that would be the greatest birthday present of all.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: If I hadn't forgotten my birthday... it's been... such a long time ago.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Do you think you could make your death less painful by taunting me?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I don't know. All you can do is, try.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Argh—*cough* *cough*

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Why—

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Why won't you die?!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *cough*... hah.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Trust me, I've tried everything I can think of.
Nowell forces down the blood that has rushed up his throat. He knows that his wounds will soon miraculously heal.
After a moment of stillness, he pushes himself up from the snow.
The pain lingers, but never on the surface.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've seen many tragedies like this one, in Victoria, Leithanien, even Gaul. What has happened to you is simply a much cleaner imitation.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: The snow will cover all dirty deeds.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Shut up—SHUT UP!!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You can hardly stand, Eroshka. Why not use that last bit of strength to hear me out?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've seen all this because I've been cursed to live forever, until I find the one thing that I can never again possess...

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: You're telling me there's something you can't find, even with a power like that?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Happiness.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: I swear, if this is some kind of joke—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I came here, because I've searched everywhere I can for the one who cursed me.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But the more I see, the more pain I feel, and the further I am from happiness and the sweet release of death.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Therefore, I won't say things like 'at least you're alive'. It's nothing to celebrate. All I can say is, at least you have a choice.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You can walk into the fire, or kill yourself some other way.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Or, if you still blame me and want to kill me, you can keep living...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: And come to find me, just as I seek the one who did this to me.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: No, don't... you can't go.

steps.name: Angry Youth
steps.text: Where will I find you?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: To tell the truth? I don't know.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: All I can give you is a token.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Ooh la la...

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I said I'd come to find you.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: This is the token you gave me.
Nowell looks at the object in the old man's hand.
It is a pair of glasses. The lenses have shattered; one side of the frame bears traces of repeated repairs, having clearly seen better days, while the other side seems good as new.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...You kept them.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Of course I did.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Did I tell you that I made them to try to end my own life?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I failed, of course.
Nowell takes the glasses and pulls out the arm on the new side.
They look at the sharp, long needle inside.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You didn't, but I can imagine.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: And they say the men of Ursus lack imagination.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: If imagination is the only way to get through certain forms of suffering, then it's a power that few in this land lack.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: True. Only imagination, but for imagination...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You polished it.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Why? It wasn't just to hold up a young girl who knew nothing, was it?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I've been looking for you. You know what this means.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You're a man of your word. You want to kill me.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Yes, but not entirely.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You've reached the age when you start to babble nonsense.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I know exactly what I'm saying.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You can choose to kill me, or you can choose not to. There is no room for ambiguity between life and death, nor is there a transitional state between them, most of the time.
Nowell reinserts the needle into the frame and gives them back to the old man.
The man snorts.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: What if I came to kill you, and save you too?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: What if I realized there wasn't anyone in particular I could hate for that tragedy... and yet I was powerless to fight the greater forces behind it?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I had some connections to this land. Then I lost it all, and there wasn't even anyone I could hate for it.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Yet you remained obsessed with looking for me, as I was once obsessed with...

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Because I was the only one who lived. I saw suffering, but I could do nothing about it. I was alive, but not truly so!

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Yes, I started to understand you. You saved me, and the thought of searching for you kept me going all these years. That's why I wanted to repay the favor.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I lived because I was cursed never to die. You lived because you were strong.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Strong. Ha, strong! Let's just say it was so.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: After you left, I was captured and sentenced to the mines, but had the good fortune to be conscripted before I came down with Oripathy.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: On the battlefield, I had my brushes with death, but each and every time I was the lucky one who lived...

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: That was when I decided I would find a method to kill anyone.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You found it, didn't you?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Yes... I think I did.
There is a light in the old man's eyes that belies his age. He grabs Nowell's hands with fire in those eyes, and puts a glass bottle in his hand.
Nowell sees a cloudy liquid swirling in the bottle.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: This is how I repay you, Nowell. No need to continue a hopeless journey in search of happiness. Drink it, and it'll all be over—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I get my revenge, you get your release.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: In alphabetical order... E... Eroshka...

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Found him! The electronic records were broken, but thankfully there were paper files.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Military backpack... bread, water bottle, two books, four medals, a photo...

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Grey jacket with a pair of glasses in the pocket, and—

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: ...Two glass bottles filled with liquid?

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: What's in the bottles? Were the bottles opened and examined, or was he asked to take a sip?

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: No... damn it, no! He got through a needle as thick as a wheat stalk—who knows what's in those bottles?!

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: He's—

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: He's with Operator Nowell, who's not carrying his Arts Unit. I have to—

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Mr. Nowell—Mr. Nowell!

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: You—
She runs out in time to see the old man's punch find Nowell's chest.
Nowell does not dodge or block and stumbles back a few steps.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *cough*—!

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Uh—

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Mr. Nowell! Are you alright?

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: What happened? Why did he hit you? Did he take out anything unusual...?
The medic operator's attention turns to the ground, where a broken glass bottle lies, its shards and a dark mark resting in the snow.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: ...Huh?
By the time she looks up, the old man has left the camp and disappeared from sight.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Are you alright, Mr. Nowell?

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Was there an altercation? Are you hurt?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...No, I'm fine.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: We—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: We just had some catching up to do.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Even you need time to think in the face of such temptation.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I understand. But we don't have much time.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: No, I'm just thinking...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: What the right way to decline is.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You no longer seek death?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Each day I long for it, more than the day before.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Then there's no reason to refuse, unless you're a coward too.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Few would describe me as brave, but that's not the reason.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You know the only thing that can kill me is happiness, Eroshka. It was a rule that an arrogant, supernatural entity imposed upon me, along with my unwilling immortality.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Now, you claim to be able to break it with a bottle of poison.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: What if I told you that you could achieve the same by taking that needle out and putting it through my temple, or neck artery?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: What...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I am no longer immortal.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: What are you trying to say?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I've seen the one who cursed me, and found what could kill me.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: The fact that I'm here now, saving lives... all of these are related.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: So you're trying to tell me that you got your revenge and found happiness here?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You found happiness in this bunch of daydreamers trying to cure the incurable?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You could say that, but the point is...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Death is already coming for me, Eroshka. If you insist that I drink this poison here and now, I will.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: The choice is yours.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: That would not be repaying you. It's just killing you.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But you'll feel better once you've found closure. There's just one pair of glasses that I still have to finish, for a girl called Katya who lives here...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Perhaps you can bring the glasses to her once I've finished them and drunk the poison.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I'll write a will, making it clear that I took my own life.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: If there's a funeral, I hope you can make it.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Ha—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Hahahahaha!

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Are you serious, Nowell? Do you think of me, the man who came to kill you, like some kind of wishing well?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I think of you as an old friend, of which I have very few.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Then you'll be disappointed, because this old friend isn't doing anything for you.
The old man snatches the bottle back from Nowell, and smashes it on the ground before he can react.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Eroshka—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I came to you with poison, and you're still trying to save me, after all these years?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Save me, comfort me, help me. It makes you happy to be in such a position, doesn't it?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Well, you're not getting your wish.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You can't save me, Nowell, because neither disease nor weapons will kill me, only the inexorable march of age—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: And if what you say is true, then you'll feel it soon enough.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Every word is true.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Whatever you say. I'll never know.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Why did you...?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Alors, when you said 'we don't have much time', what you really meant was... you don't have much time?

spans.text: Alors, when you said 'we don't have much time', what you really meant was...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You knew your days were numbered. You came to me because—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Thanks to you, I've wasted half my life, never able to repay a favor or settle a score.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Of course, you've seen many ridiculous lives like mine, in your own long, long life.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: It's not ridiculous, Eroshka, only painful.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Pain is the only thing we really can grasp in life. What's truly ridiculous... is what brought us to this point.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: It's no shame to admit the existence of pain. If I can help—is there anything I can still do for you?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: There's nothing you can do.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I can use the shards of the broken bottle, if you want.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But I don't understand. If you didn't want to grant my wish, then you should have killed me here, non? Prevent any chance that I could try to save you—

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: No. That's enough.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You know that saving lives is my life's work now.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: Fine. Stand right there, and don't move.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You changed your mind?

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: I said, stand right there—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: You're right. I'm not the one who's ridiculous, and I don't need your pity, Nowell.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: —Mr. Nowell!

steps.name: Calm Old Man
steps.text: We're square.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Mr. Nowell, Mr. Nowell?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Sorry, I was distracted. Did you say something?

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: You need to get checked, see if your ribs have cracked...

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: By the way, how are Katya's glasses going? We have to move along to the next town tomorrow morning.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: They'll be done tonight.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: Shall we go back inside the tent, then?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...You go first. I'll be fine. You know I heal quickly.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But thank you for coming to get me. I just need to clean up... the broken glass.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Can't leave them lying here. Someone, or maybe a passing burdenbeast, might accidentally step on them.
